messages.author: 1a1bcbe4d9c2ed78
messages.subject: question about db value in sound synthesis
parts:
Hi all, I'm trying to synthesize a vocalization using "synth". I need
that the relative amplitudes of different harmonics maintain the same
relation of natural vocalizations. Is there any way to enter the db
values obtained from real vocalizations ???. Thanks !!!

messages.author: acc632d9ccc1c73a
messages.subject: Re: question about db value in sound synthesis
parts:
Hi,
Down is an example how to copy an harmonic profile. However this is
done in the simplest case, ie when there is no frequency modulation.
This is might be slightly more tricky in the later case, but still
possible.
HTH
Jerome


library(seewave)
data(peewit)
# compute a spectrum in the middle of the signal
spec <- spec(peewit, at= 0.35, plot=FALSE)
# get the harmonic series
p <- fpeaks(spec, amp=c(0.01,0.01))
# synthesis of a signal with the same duration but without any AM or
FM
d <- 0.71
f <- 22050
s <- numeric(round(d*f))
for(i in 1:nrow(p))
{
h <- synth(f, d, cf = p[i,1]*1000, a = p[i,2])
s <- s + h
}
spectro(s, f)

messages.author: de80047cbc18c87e
messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Re: question about db value in sound synthesis
parts:
There is no easy way to apply a FM.

The only solution I can see is to divide the signal in different slices
and to measure the fundamental or the dominant frequency for each slice.
You then generate new slices that you eventually paste to each other.

To get a value of the dominant frequency along the signal you can use
dfreq()

data(peewit)
FM <- dfreq(peewit, at=seq(0.1, 0.6, len=10), wl=128)

You then use the different values of FM to synthesize the different
parts of the signal.

Any other idea would be very welcome!

Best

Jerome
